# k3d_argocd_application (Resource)

An Argo CD Application. Argo CD must be installed, usually with `k3d_helm_release`, and this resource should depend on it, so that it is deleted first: otherwise `cascade_delete` has no controller to finish it. Refresh only reads whether it exists and its status, because Argo CD rewrites the spec, so changes made to it outside Terraform are not detected. A private repository needs a `k3d_secret` with the label `argocd.argoproj.io/secret-type = "repository"`. Creating one that already exists fails: import it instead, with `<cluster>/<namespace>/<name>`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "k3d_argocd_application" "guestbook" {
  cluster       = k3d_cluster.main.id
  name          = "guestbook"
  wait_for_sync = true

  source = {
    repo_url        = "https://github.com/argoproj/argocd-example-apps.git"
    target_revision = "8088f4c0d970abb09e250248cc97e35623447cb5"
    path            = "guestbook"
  }

  destination = {
    namespace = "guestbook"
  }

  sync_policy = {
    automated    = true
    prune        = true
    self_heal    = true
    sync_options = ["CreateNamespace=true"]
  }

  depends_on = [k3d_helm_release.argocd]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `destination` (Attributes) Where to deploy. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--destination))
- `name` (String) Application name.
- `source` (Attributes) What to deploy. Set exactly one of `path` for a folder in a Git repository, or `chart` for a chart in a Helm repository. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--source))

### Optional

- `cascade_delete` (Boolean) Delete the deployed objects along with the Application. Defaults to `true`.
- `cluster` (String) Cluster to manage the object in, usually `k3d_cluster.<name>.id`, so the object is recreated when the cluster is replaced. Exactly one of `cluster` or `kubeconfig` is required.
- `kubeconfig` (String, Sensitive) Kubeconfig contents, for a cluster that is reached directly and not through Docker. Not recorded as a dependency on the cluster's lifetime, so prefer `cluster` for clusters in the same configuration. It is stored in Terraform state, so use an encrypted state backend.
- `namespace` (String) Namespace Argo CD runs in. Defaults to `argocd`.
- `project` (String) Argo CD project. Defaults to `default`.
- `sync_policy` (Attributes) When to sync. Left out, syncing is manual. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--sync_policy))
- `timeout` (String) How long to wait. Defaults to `5m`.
- `wait_for_sync` (Boolean) Wait until it is `Synced` and `Healthy`. Needs `sync_policy.automated`. Defaults to `false`.

### Read-Only

- `health_status` (String) Latest health status.
- `id` (String) `<cluster>/<namespace>/<name>`.
- `sync_status` (String) Latest sync status.

<a id="nestedatt--destination"></a>
### Nested Schema for `destination`

Required:

- `namespace` (String) Namespace to deploy into.

Optional:

- `server` (String) Cluster API URL. Defaults to the cluster Argo CD runs in.


<a id="nestedatt--source"></a>
### Nested Schema for `source`

Required:

- `repo_url` (String) Git or Helm repository URL.
- `target_revision` (String) Commit, tag, or chart version. A pinned value keeps deployments reproducible, so `HEAD` gives a warning.

Optional:

- `chart` (String) Chart in the Helm repository.
- `directory_recurse` (Boolean) Read manifests from subfolders of `path` too.
- `helm_release_name` (String) Helm release name. Defaults to the application name.
- `helm_values` (String) Helm values as YAML. These appear in the plan and in the Application, so reference secrets instead of including them.
- `path` (String) Folder in the Git repository.


<a id="nestedatt--sync_policy"></a>
### Nested Schema for `sync_policy`

Optional:

- `automated` (Boolean) Sync automatically when Git changes.
- `prune` (Boolean) With `automated`, delete objects removed from Git.
- `self_heal` (Boolean) With `automated`, undo changes made in the cluster.
- `sync_options` (List of String) Options such as `CreateNamespace=true`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import k3d_argocd_application.guestbook demo/argocd/guestbook
```
